narrative:
The model determined that you have a 37% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were your credit history, the loan amount requested, and the duration of the loan. Your credit history was the single most influential factor and, unfortunately, it pushed the decision toward denial. Having a history marked as "critical or other credits" is relatively common among applicants (about one in three), yet the model sees this as a warning sign compared with the majority of approved applicants who have cleanly paid existing loans.

The loan amount worked in your favor. At 2,820 DM it is slightly below the average requested by approved applicants, which helped reduce the risk score. However, the length of the loan worked against you. At 36 months it is almost twice as long as the typical 19-month duration among those who were approved, and this longer commitment increased the model's concern about repayment.

Taken together, the negative signal from your credit history outweighed the positive effect of the modest loan size, and the extended repayment period added further risk. 

To improve your chances next time, focus first on clearing any past credit issues so your history shows as "existing credits paid on time." Once that improves, consider applying for a shorter-term loan. These two changes would likely have the biggest positive impact on future decisions. (218 words)
